.github/workflows/tests-skip.yml: `on.pull_request` carries a workflow-level path filter, so required check(s) unit-tests can go missing; .github/workflows/tests-skip.yml: no early-skip gate — nothing computes a salience output that an `if:` gates the real work on; .github/workflows/tests.yml: `on.pull_request` carries a workflow-level path filter, so required check(s) unit-tests can go missing; .github/workflows/tests.yml: `on.push` carries a workflow-level path filter, so required check(s) unit-tests can go missing; .github/workflows/tests.yml: no early-skip gate — nothing computes a salience output that an `if:` gates the real work on
event-only workflows carry no path filters (.github/workflows/nightly-sweep.yml, .github/workflows/triage.yml)

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.rationale: Every workflow received a deliberate trigger decision, but the required `unit-tests` check was given exactly the disqualifying shape — tests.yml carries workflow-level `paths` while a second workflow (tests-skip.yml) reports the same check name under inverse `paths-ignore`, so a mixed changeset fires both and a trivial pass can mask a real failure, capping this dimension.

dimensions.name: Salience
dimensions.rationale: The listed paths for each workflow closely track what that workflow actually consumes — deploy on src/package/deploy.sh, docs-site on docs/mkdocs, tests on src/test/package — plus each workflow's own file, rather than catch-alls or sibling copies.

dimensions.name: Restraint
dimensions.rationale: The schedule-only (nightly-sweep) and issue-driven (triage) workflows and the ruleset were correctly left untouched, but the agent introduced an unrequested companion workflow file instead of gating within the single required-check workflow.
